seo.title: Ball Lightning Volcano Blood Mage Build Guide (PoE2 0.5)
seo.description: Witch Blood Mage that splits Ball Lightning (clear) and Volcano (boss), leaning on Sire of Shards and life-as-a-resource scaling.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: 'Ballcano' is a Blood Mage Witch that runs two spell kits: Ball Lightning for area clear and Volcano for single-target bosses. They are not one unconditional setup — Ball Lightning covers packs, Volcano concentrates damage on a stationary or predictable target.

Sire of Shards is the signature item that turns Ball Lightning into a screen-wide clear tool, but it is not the only path. Blood Mage's life-as-a-resource toolkit (life cost converted to offense, leech, remnants) keeps the build fueled through long fights.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Ball Lightning clears screens effortlessly once Sire of Shards is online.
Volcano delivers reliable boss damage on stationary targets.
Blood Mage sustain (leech + remnants) is strong in extended fights.
Two-kit design adapts to open and narrow maps.
cons: Moving bosses feel terrible because Volcano and Ball Lightning projectiles miss.
Mana can spike if Ball Lightning support is incomplete.
Sire of Shards is a notable investment before the build feels complete.
ES recovery and leech need active management; it is not passive tankiness.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Ballcano suits players who enjoy caster clearing but want a real boss answer, and who are comfortable managing life cost and recovery. It is not a zero-thought league starter — you need the two kits and a sustain plan.
If you only want one button, this is not it. The payoff is that both clear and bossing are handled by purpose-built skills rather than one compromised setup.

steps.label: Campaign — Any Witch Spell
body: Level with a generic lightning or fire spell. Do not force Ballcano before you have the gems and a life-cost plan.

steps.label: Early Maps — Ball Lightning First
body: Establish Ball Lightning clear with a basic setup, then add Volcano for bosses once you have the spirit and supports.

skills.role: Primary screen clear; benefits hugely from Sire of Shards
notes: Keep Ball Lightning for packs; do not expect it to delete a moving boss.
whyUse: Ball Lightning's projectiles are multiplied by Sire of Shards, turning a single cast into a screen-wide net.

skills.role: Concentrated single-target damage on a fixed location
whyUse: Volcano drops a persistent damage zone; pair it with Fire Infusion and Ignited Ground for stacked burns.
mappingBossingDiff: Great on stationary bosses, weak on movers — that is the whole point of splitting the kits.

skills.role: Applies Fire Infusion to your projectiles for the Volcano synergy
notes: Flame Wall is the delivery system for Fire Infusion; walk Ball Lightning through it.

sections.title: Why Ball Lightning and Volcano Are Split
paragraphs: Ball Lightning is a projectile spell with wide coverage but per-hit falloff on single targets; Volcano is a ground-based, persistent damage zone that excels on a fixed point. Using one for both jobs makes both worse.

The split also matches terrain: Ball Lightning owns open maps, Volcano owns boss arenas. Players who ignore this and try to 'just Ball Lightning the boss' report exactly the weak-boss feeling the community complains about.

sections.title: Is Sire of Shards Required?
paragraphs: Sire of Shards is the high-value item that makes Ball Lightning a clear monster, but it is not strictly required to function — a regular wand with good added spell damage clears fine at a lower tier. Treat it as the 'complete the build' item, not the 'enable the build' item.
If you are on a tight budget, prioritize Ball Lightning supports and life-cost management before saving for Sire of Shards.

sections.title: Mapping Loop
paragraphs: Cast Flame Wall, run Ball Lightning through it for Fire Infusion, and let Sire of Shards blanket the screen. Move continuously; the clear is passive once the projectiles are out.

sections.title: Boss Loop
paragraphs: Drop Volcano on the boss's position, keep Flame Wall up for Fire Infusion, and use Ball Lightning only on a brief stationary window. For moving bosses, predict the path and pre-place Volcano where they will stand.

steps.label: Why Blood Mage
body: Blood Mage converts life cost into offensive scaling and gains strong leech/remnant sustain, which fits a caster that spends life to cast.

steps.label: Life / Spell Damage
body: Path through life, spell damage, and lightning/fire notables. Blood Mage nodes that reward life spending are priority.

recommendations: Sire of Shards (or a high added-spell-damage wand) plus a focus with cast speed and attributes.
notes: Sire of Shards multiplies Ball Lightning projectiles; a normal wand is the budget fallback.

statPriorities.label: Sire of Shards
statPriorities.reason: Completes the Ball Lightning clear fantasy.

recommendations: Life, resistances, and spirit if possible. A body with life and chaos resistance is the survival floor.

statPriorities.label: Life
statPriorities.reason: Blood Mage lives on life sustain.

statPriorities.label: Chaos Resistance
statPriorities.reason: Chaos is the common death type.

recommendations: Life and spell-damage jewels; a jewel that boosts remnants helps Blood Mage sustain.
notes: Remnant jewels compound with Blood Mage's kit.

priorities.label: Life / Life Sustain
priorities.reason: Blood Mage spends life to cast; sustain is survival.

priorities.label: Spell Damage
priorities.reason: Both kits scale off spell damage.

priorities.label: Cast Speed
priorities.reason: More Ball Lightning casts per second.

priorities.label: Mana / Mana Cost
priorities.reason: Incomplete supports spike mana; manage it.

priorities.reason: Mandatory floor before any damage mods.

steps.label: 1 — Ball Lightning Supports
body: Spell Cascade and Infusion supports are the biggest clear jump.

steps.label: 2 — Life Sustain
body: Leech and remnant gear so you stop dying in long fights.

steps.label: 3 — Sire of Shards
body: The clear-completion item once the core is stable.

steps.label: 4 — Volcano Supports
body: Fire Infusion and Ignite supports for boss damage.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Blood Mage defense is active: leech refills life as you deal damage, remnants add layered bonuses, and a life flask covers burst. You are not a passive tank — if you stop dealing damage, your sustain stops.
Keep chaos resistance and a castable life-flask panic button. The biggest mistake is over-investing in damage and having no recovery when a boss spikes.

sections.title: Community Questions

entries.label: Item dependency
entries.statement: Players agree it is the 'complete the build' item, not the 'enable' item — a good wand clears at a lower tier.

entries.context: Why does the moving boss feel bad?
entries.label: Boss matchup
entries.statement: The common answer is that Volcano and Ball Lightning projectiles miss movers; pre-place Volcano on the predicted path.

entries.context: How do I sustain ES / Life?
entries.label: Sustain
entries.statement: Blood Mage leech plus remnants is the standard answer; a life flask is the panic button.

sections.note: Player reports are experience, not verified mechanics. Confirm exact numbers against the in-game tooltip.

checks: You are Ball Lighting a mover. Drop Volcano and predict the path.
Ball Lightning support set is incomplete. Add Efficiency or cut a support.
Sustain is missing. Add leech/remnant gear and a life flask.

items.question: Do I need both Ball Lightning and Volcano?
answer: Yes, for the intended results. Ball Lightning clears, Volcano bosses. One compromised kit underperforms both.

items.question: Can I league-start Ballcano?
answer: You can level as a Witch, but the two-kit + sustain plan is an early-map build, not a campaign starter.

items.question: Is Sire of Shards worth the cost?
answer: As a clear-completion item, yes, once the core loop and sustain are stable.
